key_points: Q3 GDPNow at ~5.1% annualized and initial claims at 196k signal a re-accelerating economy driven by AI capex and resilient spending.
Strong growth plus a Fed that just hiked unanimously to 3.75-4% keeps a mild upward bias on yields, though 2y at 4.76 already prices several more hikes, limiting the 3m edge at the front end.
Hiking cycle into strong growth favors continued bear-flattening near term; the 2s10s spread is at its 1y low.
Earnings/growth backdrop supportive for equities and tight HY spreads, but valuations and rising real rates cap the edge; VIX near the bottom of its range has mild mean-reversion risk.
Consumer sentiment at 51.7 and $100 oil are the drag on low/middle-income households, a downside risk to growth further out.
Rising real yields and a firm dollar on growth/rate differentials weigh on gold; oil after a 26% 3m run has less growth-driven upside.
August CPI rose about 0.4% m/m and is about 3.35% y/y. Core PCE is about 3.35% y/y. Inflation is elevated, broad-based and reinforced by WTI above $100 (+17% in 1m).
The Fed hiked unanimously to 3.75-4% and dropped the 'supply shock' framing, saying only 'Inflation remains elevated'. That is a hawkish reaction function, so the front end keeps a mild upward bias.
2y at 4.76 already prices roughly three more hikes. With yields at 1y highs, the edge is small and mean reversion limits conviction.
Inflation-driven tightening tends to bear-flatten the curve. 2s10s is at its 1y low, but the lean is still toward further flattening.
The 10y breakeven is stable at 2.33 despite the oil surge, which reflects Fed credibility. Oil pass-through is offset by tightening, so the breakeven call is neutral.
Higher real yields and a firm dollar weigh on gold. The policy-rate differential supports the dollar.

Ongoing tightening into an inflation shock is a headwind for very rich equity valuations. With VIX near 1y lows and HY spreads near tights, risks skew toward wider spreads and higher volatility over 1-3m.
Labor market is firm and modestly tightening: payrolls +162k in August, unemployment steady at 4.1% (down from 4.3% a year ago), initial claims at a very low 196k.
Tight labor plus elevated inflation keeps the Fed's hiking bias alive after the unanimous September hike; supports a mild upward tilt to front-end yields and continued curve flattening.
Yields already at 1y highs and 2y futures shorts at the 99th percentile limit the edge; much of the hawkish labor story is priced, risk of short-covering rallies.
Strong employment underpins earnings and credit quality, keeping HY spreads tight and equities supported, though VIX near 1y lows leaves room for mean reversion higher over longer horizons.
Higher real yields on tight-labor-driven Fed tightening are a mild headwind for gold; little direct labor signal for oil or breakevens.
Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 by a unanimous vote, after three hawkish dissents in July. 'The Committee will deliver price stability' signals a credible tightening bias.

At 4.76%, the 2-year yield sits about 90bp above the funds rate, so the market already prices several more hikes. That is a lot priced against a statement with no explicit forward guidance, giving modest mean-reversion odds for the 2-year at 1m and 3m.
A hiking cycle tends to keep the 2s10s curve flat near term. If front-end pricing proves excessive, some steepening is possible later.
Rate differentials versus advanced foreign economies widen in the U.S.' favor, supporting the dollar. Rising real yields weigh on gold.
A credible, hawkish Fed keeps long-run breakevens anchored, as the minutes note, and leans against further oil-driven inflation repricing.

Tightening into elevated equity valuations and historically tight credit spreads (HY spread at the 8th percentile, VIX at the 6th) skews risk toward wider spreads and higher volatility over 1m and 3m.
Upcoming catalysts: Sep minutes on Oct 7, the Oct 28 FOMC, and the Dec 9 SEP. The Dec dots will test whether the Fed validates the market's hike path.

Fiscal/supply lens: 10y at 5.01%, top of 1y range, with real-yield-driven selloff; heavy coupon supply and an elevated term premium keep a mild upward bias on long yields, though 5% attracts duration demand.

November quarterly refunding falls inside the 3m window; any hint of larger coupon sizes would add term premium and steepen the curve, so 2s10s tilts higher at longer horizons despite Fed-driven bear flattening recently.

Front end is policy-driven (Fed hiked to 3.75-4%); spec 2y shorts already covered to 99th percentile, leaving little supply-based edge on DGS2; Fed bill purchases for reserve management modestly absorb bill supply.

Post-September tax date TGA rebuild and fiscal year-end flows are a minor liquidity drain; rising long yields are a valuation headwind for equities with tight HY spreads and low VIX vulnerable to a term-premium shock.
Fiscal-credibility concerns slightly favor gold and slightly weigh on the dollar over 1-3m; breakevens and oil have no clear fiscal-supply signal.

The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September. Yet financial conditions remain loose: NFCI is at -0.56, the HY spread is 2.68% (8th percentile) and VIX is 14.8 (6th percentile). The Committee may want tighter conditions, which skews spreads and VIX modestly upward over 1-3 months.

The balance sheet is still growing slowly through reserve-management bill purchases. Reserves are ample and repo was only briefly soft, so there are no funding-stress signals and no near-term liquidity shock.

The 2-year at 4.76% sits about 90bp above the funds-rate midpoint and already prices several more hikes. Spec shorts in 2-year notes are being covered. Room for further front-end repricing looks limited, so I lean slightly toward lower 2-year yields at 3 months.
The curve is flattening (2s10s at 0.25%, a 1-year low) under hikes. That trend can extend near term, but it is stretched.
The widening U.S. rate gap and foreign inflows into U.S. equities support the dollar mildly.
Rising real yields weigh on gold. Oil at about $101 is expected by Fed staff to ease. Breakevens are anchored by perceived Fed resolve.

Equities have positive drift because credit is available and bank lending standards are easing. That is offset by stretched valuations and hedge fund leverage near records, which is a tail risk if conditions tighten.

Yields sit at 1-year highs (100th percentile) after a hike; 2y spec net short is the least extreme in a year after +74k covering, so squeeze fuel is limited, but stretched levels argue mild mean reversion lower.
2s10s at the 0th percentile of its range; a crowded flattening move leaves modest room for re-steepening over longer horizons.
VIX at 14.8 (6th percentile) with VIX futures specs heavily net short: complacency and short-vol crowding skew risks toward a vol pickup over 1-3 months.
HY OAS at 2.68% (8th percentile) is priced for perfection amid hedge-fund leverage near records; asymmetric widening risk.
ES specs net short (-100k) is a contrarian support for equities despite rich valuations; low vol regimes tend to drift higher.
Gold spec length at the 80th percentile despite weak price is crowded; oil longs are moderate after a +17% month, implying fading momentum risk.
Dollar spec longs trimmed and positioning moderate: no strong edge.

Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% while most AFE central banks held; the widening US-foreign rate gap and resilient US growth keep supporting foreign inflows and the dollar, which sits only mid-range (45th pct) despite record-high US yields — room to catch up.

2y at 4.76% already prices roughly three to four more hikes above the funds midpoint; with record speculative shorts in TU (99th pct), the front end looks over-extended, so we lean to 2y yields fading and the curve re-steepening over 3m.
Global sovereign yields rising in tandem with US yields limits the scope for a sharp 10y rally; 10y momentum at a 1y high but mostly priced.
Strong dollar and high real yields are headwinds for gold (already -10% y/y) and, at the margin, for dollar-priced oil after a +17% month; Middle East supply risk keeps oil two-sided.

Foreign equity inflows support the S&P, but tight HY spreads (8th pct) and low VIX (6th pct) leave asymmetric risk of widening/vol spikes from global shocks (Asian semis valuations, geopolitics) at longer horizons.

WTI at $101, +17% in a month and +59% y/y on Middle East conflict; geopolitical supply-premium spikes tend to mean-revert and the curve is likely backwardated, so spot drift skews lower over 1-3 months, with fat upside tails if escalation continues.
Specs are only moderately long crude (66th percentile), leaving limited squeeze fuel but no extreme crowding either.

Oil pass-through has shown up in nominal and real yields and Fed hikes rather than breakevens; a fading oil premium would trim front-end hike pricing and breakevens, modestly favoring lower 2y yields and some steepening at 3m.
Gold has failed to rally despite the oil shock because rising real rates and Fed tightening dominate; spec long at 80th percentile caps upside.

Energy-driven inflation hurts low-income consumers (sentiment 51.7) but equities remain supported by AI capex; tight HY spreads and VIX near lows leave asymmetric risk of widening and a VIX rise if the oil shock escalates.
The Middle East conflict is the dominant geopolitical driver. WTI at $101 after +17% in a month embeds a large risk premium that is vulnerable to de-escalation, though re-escalation tails remain.

The VIX at the 6th percentile and HY spreads at the 8th percentile look complacent given the conflict, the Fed hiking and AI-valuation fragility. That skews vol and spreads modestly higher over 1-3 months.

An oil shock plus a hawkish Fed (unanimous hike, 'will deliver price stability') favors bear-flattening. A geopolitical risk-off episode would instead pull 10y yields down from 1y highs; the net lean is slightly lower yields at 3m.
The dollar gets mild support from safe-haven demand and the widening rate gap versus AFEs. Gold has been undercut by rising real yields but retains geopolitical hedge value.
Breakevens have shown limited sensitivity to oil because of Fed credibility. With oil premium fade risk, they lean slightly lower over longer horizons.
Equities sit near highs with solid growth. Geopolitical shocks are tail risks rather than the base case, so a mild upward drift is retained.

thesis: The Fed hiked unanimously to 3.75-4.00% into strong growth (GDPNow about 5%, claims 196k) with inflation elevated (core PCE about 3.3-3.4%) and oil at $101. Rates sit at 1y highs: the 2-year is about 90bp above the funds midpoint, pricing roughly three more hikes, and specs covered heavily in TU. Front-end edge is therefore slight mean reversion lower at 3m, and 10-year yields are roughly coin-flip. The 2s10s curve is at its 1y low; bear-flattening may persist near term, with mild re-steepening odds by 3m around the refunding and any repricing of the front end. The dollar has mild support from rate differentials, though it is mid-range. Equities keep positive drift on earnings, AI capex and foreign inflows despite rich valuations. HY spreads (8th percentile) and VIX (6th percentile) are complacent against Fed tightening and geopolitical risk, so I skew both modestly higher over 1-3m. The oil geopolitical premium after a +17% month leans toward fading, with fat upside tails. Gold is pressured by real yields but positioned long, so roughly neutral-slightly down. Breakevens stay anchored by Fed credibility, leaning slightly lower if oil fades.
